findings: Learner overview: “its earliest cited oracle-bone use is a place name” makes the historical caveat dominate the first-reading explanation. Lead with the supported picture and common meaning; keep the place-name qualification in the detailed history. Suggested overview: “老 pictures a bent, long-haired person with a staff and commonly means ‘old’ or ‘aged.’” Cite the pictographic interpretation and current meaning (for example, X-3f72174484566c025046 and X-a560c34133b8998b3005).
